subject.title: MCP retry storm can exhaust VM resources; need backoff, circuit breaker, and default systemd guardrails

question: Which host-safety boundary should OpenClaw guarantee for repeatedly failing MCP servers: runtime failed-start circuiting only, or runtime circuiting plus installer-owned systemd resource ceilings?
rationale: The runtime breaker is a clear safety repair, but service memory/task limits, OOM priority, and swap policy can intentionally stop existing workloads or alter the host outside OpenClaw; repository evidence does not establish an approved default policy.

options.title: Runtime breaker plus conservative service caps
options.body: Implement process-wide failed-start suppression and add upgrade-safe systemd task and memory ceilings with doctor diagnostics and operator override guidance.

options.title: Runtime breaker only
options.body: Guarantee bounded MCP spawning in core while leaving host resource ceilings as documented operator-controlled hardening.

options.title: Observe and document
options.body: Keep current cleanup and short pauses, adding only diagnostics and manual service guidance without failed-start enforcement.

recommendation.title: Runtime breaker plus conservative service caps
recommendation.body: Implement process-wide failed-start suppression and add upgrade-safe systemd task and memory ceilings with doctor diagnostics and operator override guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest concrete history signal is the merged commit that introduced the affected bundled MCP runtime and subprocess lifecycle.
